title: security-and-compliance-rbac-auth-audit-data-residency-retention-sdlc-incident-response-evidence-risk-exceptions-2025-09-15
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's core security and compliance controls and procedures across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is the single-source reference for engineering, security, and compliance teams when implementing, reviewing, or auditing controls.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood-managed services (hosted API, dedicated, private control plane), developer tooling, CI/CD pipelines, and supporting infrastructure.

Owners and escalation
---------------------
- Document owner: Security (Sofia Martinez)
- Primary operational owner (logs & retention): Eng Platform (Liam Chen)
- Incident response lead: Eng SRE on-call; backup: Security on-call
- Compliance evidence owner: Legal & Compliance (Priya Rao)

1) RBAC & Authentication
------------------------
Intro
: RBAC and authentication are enforced consistently across control plane and tenant planes. The objective is least privilege, separation of duties, and auditable role assignments.

Roles and role model
- Global roles: Platform Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, Support Engineer, SRE, Developer, Read-only Auditor
- Resource-scoped roles: Model-Onboarder, Dedicated-Operator, Private-Deployment-Admin, Observability-Viewer
- Principle of least privilege: roles must be scoped to the minimum resource set and permissions required.

Authentication mechanisms
- SSO (OIDC/SAML) via enterprise identity providers (Okta, Azure AD). SSO is the primary authentication method for all human users.
- Enforced MFA for all interactive logins (TOTP or WebAuthn).
- Service principals (short-lived tokens) for machine-to-machine: issued by the internal Token Service with TTL <= 24h by default.
- Key material: long-lived keys are prohibited for service accounts; where unavoidable, store in KMS/HSM and rotate quarterly.

Access lifecycle (onboard/offboard/change)
1. Access request initiated via access request portal (link: /access-requests).
2. Approver (owner team) validates business need; assigns scoped role.
3. Grant is time-bound; maximum 90 days without renewal.
4. Offboard: HR/People-ops trigger account disable; automation removes group memberships and revokes tokens within 1 hour.

Policies and enforcement
- Role assignment is group-based (SCIM-managed groups where supported).
- Periodic access review cadence: quarterly for privileged roles; annual for non-privileged roles.
- RBAC drift detection: weekly inventory job reports unexpected privileges; severity-high findings create Jira ticket to owner.

Auditability
- All role changes, group membership changes, and token issuances are logged to the audit pipeline (see Audit Logging section).

2) Audit logging
----------------
Objectives
- Provide a tamper-evident, searchable record of security-relevant events to support investigations, compliance attestations, and SLOs.

What we log (minimum)
- Authentication events: login successes/failures, MFA events, token issuance and revocations.
- Authorization events: role grant/revoke, policy changes, scope changes.
- Administrative actions: user/group creation, secret rotations, KMS policy changes.
- Data access events: model download, dataset exports, config downloads.
- System events: pipeline deployments, infra changes, job executions relevant to security posture.

Event schema (example)
- Each audit record includes: timestamp, event_id, actor (user/service), actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success/failure), request_ip, request_agent, correlation_id, raw_payload

Example JSON event:
{
  "timestamp": "2025-09-15T14:12:03Z",
  "event_id": "evt_01G8X2Y9QWZ3A0",
  "actor": "user:sofia.martinez@redwood.ai",
  "actor_id": "usr-0a1b2c",
  "action": "role.grant",
  "resource_type": "group",
  "resource_id": "grp-model-onboarders",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_ip": "203.0.113.45",
  "correlation_id": "corr-1234abcd",
  "raw_payload": "{...}"
}

Log pipeline and retention
- Ingestion: agents forward structured audit events (JSON) to a central collector (Kafka topic: audit-events-prod).
- Storage/Indexing: Archive raw events to encrypted object storage (S3: s3://redwood-audit-archive/prod/) and index to SIEM (Splunk/Elastic).
- Tamper-evidence: write-once manifests and periodic checksum verification jobs (daily).
- Retention policy:
  - Critical security audit logs: 7 years (regulated customers).
  - Standard audit logs: 2 years on hot index (searchable), 7 years in cold archive (object storage).
  - Access logs (low-sensitivity): 1 year.

SLOs and operational metrics
- Ingestion availability: 99.9% (monthly).
- Event delivery latency to SIEM: P95 < 30s.
- Archive durability: 99.999999999% (as provided by cloud provider).

Access and monitoring
- Read access to audit indices is privileged: Security and Compliance teams by default; Read-only Auditor role for approved requests.
- Alerts: anomalous auth spikes, grant-to-service-account ratio changes, and evidence of deletion of audit manifests trigger high-severity alerts.

3) Data residency & retention
-----------------------------
Principles
- Customers may select region(s) for their data residency (US, EU, APAC where supported).
- Default encryption-at-rest and in-transit for all customer data.

Residency controls
- Tenant data is partitioned by region at the storage layer. Cross-region replication is disabled by default; enabled only with explicit customer consent and documented risk acceptance.
- Audit logs and telemetry are stored in the customer-selected region unless the customer opts into centralized analytics.

Retention rules (summary table described)
- Table: data type | default retention | long-term archive | owner
  - Customer Content | 30 days | 7 years (by request) | Customer Data Team
  - Audit Logs | 2 years (hot), 7 years (archive) | 7 years | Security
  - Metrics/Telemetry | 90 days (detailed), 3 years (aggregates) | 3 years | Observability
  - Backups / Snapshots | 30 days | 1 year (per customer SLA) | Eng Infra

Retention configuration (example YAML)
retention_policies:
  - name: customer_content
    default_days: 30
    archive_days: 2555  # 7 years
  - name: audit_logs
    hot_days: 730
    cold_archive_days: 2555

Encryption and key management
- Customer data is encrypted with CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) where requested.
- KMS key rotation: automatic every 90 days for platform-managed keys; customers manage CMEK per their policies.

4) Secure SDLC
---------------
Objectives
- Integrate security controls into the software lifecycle to prevent, detect, and remediate vulnerabilities prior to production.

Gates and tooling
- Pre-commit: dependency vulnerability scanning (dependabot/renovate + internal checks).
- CI: SAST (static analysis), secret scanning, license compliance, container image vulnerability scanning. Failing SAST blocks merge.
- PR review: security checklist must be completed for services touching customer data or infra.
- Staging: DAST + auth smoke tests + canary rollout to limited capacity.
- Production rollout: gradual ramp with automated rollback on error budget or regression signals.

Developer responsibilities
- Every repo must include SECURITY.md and a threat model for services in scope.
- All third-party code must be approved via dependency policy; high-risk libraries require architecture review.

CI/CD controls
- Signing: production artifacts (containers, binaries) are signed and provenance recorded.
- Least privilege for CI service accounts: ephemeral runner tokens, least-scope secrets.
- Immutable artifacts: no direct modification in production; patches require new artifact build and redeploy.

5) Incident response — security procedures
-----------------------------------------
Goals
- Contain incidents quickly, preserve forensic evidence, communicate with stakeholders, and remediate root causes.

Severity classification (summary)
- Sev-1 (Critical): active data exfiltration, customer-impacting production outage for >30m, compromised keys.
- Sev-2 (High): confirmed unauthorized access with limited scope, failed backups for >24h.
- Sev-3 (Medium): suspicious activity requiring investigation.

Playbook (high level)
1. Detection and Triage
   - Automated alerts from SIEM, IDS, or observability trigger initial triage by on-call SRE.
   - Create incident record (Jira/Incident system) with initial classification and timeline.
2. Containment
   - Apply immediate short-term controls: rotate affected keys, revoke compromised tokens, isolate affected hosts or clusters.
   - Preserve volatile evidence: snapshot disks, collect memory if required.
3. Eradication and Recovery
   - Apply fixes (patch, config change), validate in staging, then roll to production with monitoring.
4. Forensics and root cause analysis
   - Security performs forensic analysis; all actions logged and copies of logs preserved to secure evidence store.
5. Communication
   - Internal: incident channel in Slack and regular briefings for execs.
   - External: coordinate with Legal & Comms for customer notifications per contractual and regulatory timelines.
6. Post-incident actions
   - Postmortem within 7 days; include corrective actions, owners, and deadlines.

Evidence preservation
- Evidence store: encrypted object storage with restricted access; retention: 7 years for incidents affecting data exfiltration.
- Chain-of-custody: record who accessed evidence, when, and for what purpose.

6) Compliance evidence workflows
--------------------------------
Objective
- Provide repeatable procedures to collect artifacts required for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).

Evidence categories and owners
- Policy artifacts: this document, control matrices — owner: Security
- Technical artifacts: config exports, access logs, deployment manifests — owner: Eng Platform
- Operational artifacts: incident postmortems, oncall rotations, access review records — owner: Eng SRE and Security

Workflow (example for SOC2 scoping)
1. Evidence request received by Compliance (ticket).
2. Compliance assigns artifact owners and due dates.
3. Owners gather artifacts, annotate with collection method and timeframe.
4. Artifacts uploaded to evidence portal (immutable) with checksum and collection metadata.
5. Independent reviewer (internal auditor) performs spot validation.

Checklist for artifact submission
- Include: artifact description, time range, collection command or UI path, responsible owner, verification steps.
- Example command to export auth logs:
  curl -u "svc-evidence-token:REDACTED" "https://audit-api.redwood.internal/v1/logs?from=2025-06-01&to=2025-06-30" -o auth-logs-june-2025.json

Retention of evidence
- Evidence for completed audits: retain for 7 years unless otherwise required.

7) Risk & exceptions
---------------------
Principles
- Exceptions to policy are permissible only with documented risk acceptance and compensating controls. Exceptions are time-boxed and subject to renewal.

Exception request process
1. Submit exception request via the risk register (link: /risk-register) including: scope, rationale, compensating controls, proposed duration (<= 90 days for high-risk).
2. Risk review: Security + Owning engineering team assess risk and recommend controls.
3. Approvals: Security lead and either CTO or Legal depending on customer/regulatory impact.
4. Monitor: automated checks run weekly for high-risk exceptions and report status.

Exception template (required fields)
- request_id, requester, service_affected, requested_change, business_justification, compensating_controls, start_date, end_date, approvers, renewal_date

Renewal and closure
- Renewal required at least 7 days before end_date. Exceptions automatically expire at end_date; expired exceptions generate a blocking ticket for remediation.
